content_metadata.description: Analysis of a Terminix commercial featuring exaggerated termite creatures to highlight the threat termites pose to homes.

qAndA.answer: The commercial states that termites can cause up to $8,600 in damage.
qAndA.question: How much damage can termites cause?

qAndA.answer: Terminix offers the 'Ultimate Protection Guarantee' to combat termites.
qAndA.question: What is the Terminix solution offered in the ad?

qAndA.answer: The creatures are designed to be unsettling and destructive, visually representing the fear and anxiety associated with termite infestations.
qAndA.question: How does the visual style of the creatures contribute to the ad's message?

qAndA.answer: The commercial aims to evoke feelings of unease, anxiety, and urgency, prompting viewers to take action against potential termite problems.
qAndA.question: What is the overall mood the commercial aims to evoke?

qAndA.answer: The transition from a large, destructive creature to a smaller, unseen creature in a typical home setting personalizes the threat, making it more relatable and concerning for viewers.
qAndA.question: How does the transition from the first scene to the second scene affect the narrative?

activities.description: Termite Creature 1 flies through a neighborhood, destroying houses.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The termites are a metaphor for a hidden problem that can quickly escalate and cause extensive damage if left unchecked.

mood.description: Anxious, Tense. The sudden appearance of the creature, the destruction, the fast cuts, and the dramatic music all contribute to a feeling of anxiety and danger.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Shift from black and white to color as the creature appears, marking a stark transition from calm to chaotic.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of a destructive force (Termite Creature 1) that causes significant damage to homes.

scenes.thematicElements: Destruction, vulnerability of homes, the unseen threat.
scenes.title: Scene 1

videoEditingDetails.description: Transition to full color as the creature appears, emphasizing the destructive force.
POV shot through a window as the creature approaches.
Quick cuts and fast-paced editing to increase tension and chaos.

activities.description: Termite Creature 2 chews on a wooden support beam in a basement.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Just as the creature is hidden in the basement, termites often go unnoticed until they have caused significant damage.

mood.description: Uneasy, Disconcerting. The creature's unsettling appearance, the confined space of the basement, and the sound of chewing create a feeling of discomfort.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The camera cuts to a close-up of the infested beam, highlighting the hidden damage and increasing the feeling of unease.

narrativeProgression.description: A second, more insidious threat (Termite Creature 2) is introduced, demonstrating the damage termites can cause in a typical home setting.

props.name: Basement setting with a washer, dryer, water heater.

scenes.thematicElements: Hidden threats, the importance of home protection, proactive prevention.
scenes.title: Scene 2

videoEditingDetails.description: Close-up shot of the damaged beam, emphasizing the termites' work.

climax.description: There isn't a traditional climax. The commercial aims to create a sense of urgency and unease that prompts viewers to take action against termites.

storylines.description: The commercial uses exaggerated creatures to represent the very real threat termites pose to homes. It highlights both the visible and hidden damage they can cause.

content_metadata.title: Terminix Commercial Analysis

trimmingSuggestions.description: Shortening or removing the initial black and white segment would create a more attention-grabbing opening.
A faster cut between the scenes would maintain the commercial's energy and urgency.

Tvcs X 2 :30, :15
Agency: PUBLICIS DALLAS
Director: DVEIN
Production: BLACKLIST
Animation: DVEIN VANDO FURIA http://www.dvein.com http://www.vandostudio.com http://www.furia-digital.com

Dvein enlists fellow Barcelonians Vando Studio and Furia Digital to construct this visual metaphor for how incredibly destructive termites really are. "Initially, the storyline was about monsters flying over a town, turning into termites. But then we thought 'Why not show monsters causing direct damage to the houses?' The agency fully supported this idea and we developed it further with them.

"The monster design was our first challenge: developing a 3D creature away from the typical blockbuster, high-budget movies; we needed to create a characteristic identity that distinguished the commercial, that made it atypical.

"We decided to work with real land animals who are massive, like buffalos and elephants in a stampede, but which can also fly. We were searching for something unexpected and at the same time it had to have the insects features, but magnified.

"The idea was building a collage of attitudes, forms and textures that were also the projection of a termite's modus operandi. At the same time, our ideas had to go in the same direction as the client's, but without losing the organic forms of Dvein's signature.

"Once every monster was finished, we got into the animation process. Our main aim was to translate truthfully every detail of the monster into movement, transmitting the fast and action-packed rhythm of the commercial. We had only 10 seconds to show the monsters' capacity to fly, but also to destruct. The destruction feeling was very important, not only in the way that the monsters destroyed the houses but in the way the houses rupture.

"At the same time, we didn't want to lose the modeling and texturing details, so we chose to have a slow-motion sequence, that allows appreciating those details but at the same time adds drama to the story. Dynamics simulation tools as well as manual animation were required to achieve this.

"We were also very accurate in choosing the framing. We wanted to amplify the sensation of weight and clearly appreciate the anatomy of the monsters so we had to locate the cameras in strategic points to give the whole scene a deeper realism.

"In the second commercial we wanted to focus on the termites' most specific and basic feature: they eat. They eat a lot, especially wood. For this reason, we worked specifically with the mouth, almost a mouth with legs, but which also had saw characteristics."
